title: Stability transfers across a weakly stable dense extension
statement: Let $K\subseteq F$ be fields [def-weil-field] with compatible nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute values. Assume $K$ is dense in $F$: for every $x\in F$ and $\epsilon>0$ there is $a\in K$ with $|x-a|_F<\epsilon$. Assume $K$ is stable [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field]. Assume also the following weak stability condition on $F$: for every finite extension $E/F$, endowed with its minimal-polynomial spectral norm $s_{E/F}$ [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm], and every $F$-basis $w_1,\ldots,w_m$ of $E$, there exist real constants $c,C>0$ such that $$c\max_i |a_i|_F\ \le\ s_{E/F}\left(\sum_i a_iw_i\right)\ \le\ C\max_i |a_i|_F\qquad(a_i\in F).$$ Then $F$ is stable [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field]. No completeness of $K$ or $F$, algebraicity of $F/K$, or separability of the finite extensions is assumed.

proof.text: Put $H=\widehat K$. By [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion] this is a complete field with an isometric copy of $K$, and [lem-trf-stable-field-completion] makes $H$ stable. For $x\in F$, choose $a_m\in K$ with $|x-a_m|_F<2^{-m}$ and map $x$ to the Cauchy class $(a_m)$ in $H$. The ultrametric inequality makes this sequence Cauchy and makes the class independent of the choices. Approximants for $x+y$ and $xy$ can be taken to be $a_m+b_m$ and $a_mb_m$: convergent sequences are bounded and $|a_mb_m-xy|\le\max(|a_m||b_m-y|,|y||a_m-x|)\to0$. This proves additivity and multiplicativity, and constant sequences give preservation of $1$. Taking limits of absolute values proves isometry and hence injectivity. Thus regard $K\subseteq F\subseteq H$ isometrically. The image of $F$ is dense since it contains $K$. Its metric completion is therefore $H$: send a Cauchy sequence in $F$ to its limit in $H$; this is an isometry, and surjectivity follows already from the Cauchy sequences in $K$. The absolute value on $H$ is nonarchimedean by taking limits of the inequality on $K$, and nontrivial because it restricts to the given value on $K$.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary finite extension $E/F$ of dimension $n\ge1$, and write $s=s_{E/F}$. It is a definite ultrametric $F$-algebra norm by [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm]. Choose any basis of $E/F$; the assumed weak stability supplies its positive constants $c,C$. Apply [lem-trf-weak-spectral-completion-product], using the identified completion $H=\widehat F$. We obtain the $n$-dimensional $H$-algebra $A=\widehat E$, with norm $N=\widehat s$, an isometric dense inclusion $E\hookrightarrow A$, and an isometric product decomposition $A\simeq\prod_{j=1}^r L_j$ with norm $\max_j s_{L_j/H}$. In particular we have used no separability and have not asserted that $A$ is a field.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.2/3, printed p.158 (scan PDF p.166), completion criterion; proof supplied by the agent because the local archival document is absent.

proof.text: Since $H$ is stable, [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field] supplies an orthogonal spectral $H$-basis of each finite field $L_j/H$. Insert each such basis into the $j$th product coordinate, with zero in the other coordinates, and pull back along the product isomorphism from step 2. These vectors form an $H$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $A$: spanning and independence follow coordinate by coordinate, and the number of vectors is $\sum_j[L_j:H]=n$. For any scalars $h_i\in H$, the product maximum formula and the orthogonal formula within each factor give $$N\left(\sum_i h_i b_i\right)=\max_i |h_i|N(b_i).$$ Each weight $d_i=N(b_i)$ is positive because the vectors are nonzero. This is an exact orthogonal basis; no almost-orthogonal estimate is substituted.

proof.text: By density of $E$ in $A$, choose $v_i\in E$ with $N(v_i-b_i)<d_i$ for every $i$. Set $\delta=\max_i N(v_i-b_i)/d_i<1$. For scalars $a_i\in F$, not all zero, put $M=\max_i |a_i|d_i>0$. The ultrametric and scalar axioms of the norm give $$N\left(\sum_i a_i(v_i-b_i)\right)\le\max_i |a_i|N(v_i-b_i)\le\delta M<M,$$ whereas step 3 gives $N(\sum_i a_ib_i)=M$. In any ultrametric norm, $N(y)<N(x)$ implies $N(x+y)=N(x)$: the upper bound is $N(x+y)\le N(x)$, and a strict inequality would contradict $N(x)\le\max(N(x+y),N(y))$. Hence $s(\sum_i a_iv_i)=N(\sum_i a_iv_i)=M$. Applying the same argument to just the $i$th coefficient gives $s(v_i)=d_i$. Thus $$s\left(\sum_i a_iv_i\right)=\max_i|a_i|s(v_i),$$ including the all-zero tuple. The formula makes the $v_i$ linearly independent over $F$; there are $n=\dim_F E$ of them, so they form a basis. This proves the condition of [def-trf-stable-nonarchimedean-field] for the arbitrary $E/F$, and therefore proves stability of $F$.
